newsitem.title: UK: CE says Northern H1 results are "lacklustre".
newsitem.headline: CE says Northern H1 results are "lacklustre".

text.p: U.S. energy group CE Electric said half year profits reported by its bid target Northern Electric were "lacklustre."
"Despite throwing in the kitchen sink, these results are lacklustre," a spokesman for CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, said.
Northern brought out results early as part of its defence against CE Electric's $1.225 billion bid which values it at 630 pence per share.

The regional electricity company said pretax profits for the six months ending September 30 were 50.7 million stg, down from 58.7 million stg as a price review which came into effect in April 1996 made an impact.
It paid out an interim dividend of 12.85 pence, up from 12.0 pence previously and forecast full year pretax profits would be over 112 million stg with a forecast dividend of 29.85 pence per share.
It said gearing would be around 95 percent by March 31 after paying out a special dividend which is part of a defence package used to fend off Trafalgar House, now part of Kvaerner, last year.
